sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Ava Berger
articles.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.
articles.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend

articles.author: Chiara Eisner
articles.description: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
articles.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows

articles.author: Saige Miller
articles.description: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.
articles.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.
articles.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that

articles.author: Justin Chang
articles.description: Lee Chang-dong's novelistic drama tells the story of two very different couples who meet during the filming of a documentary.
articles.title: 'Possible Love' offers four of the best performances you'll see all year

articles.author: Glen Weldon
articles.description: Like its protagonist, the film shoots out its goopy, mud-brown, protoplasmic feelers into the undiscovered territory of horror, but it does so too tentatively.
articles.title: 'Clayface' is underbaked body horror

articles.author: Ryan Lucas
articles.description: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.
articles.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries

articles.author: Jonathan Lambert
articles.description: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?
articles.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia

articles.author: Kate Bartlett
articles.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.
articles.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
articles.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack

articles.author: David Smith in Austin, Texas
articles.description:
The Senate candidate denounced opponent Ken Paxton, calling out corruption allegations and support from Musk
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Texas, has taken aim at Elon Musk, warning that the tech mogul is trying to buy political influence and declaring: “Texas is not for sale.”
Talarico held a campaign rally on Friday at the University of Texas at Austin, packing an auditorium at his alma mater with hundreds of students and other supporters, who cheered, whooped and waved campaign signs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat James Talarico targets Elon Musk at rally: ‘Texas is not for sale’

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Super typhoon weakening but large parts of Taiwan, including Taipei, still mostly closed and flights cancelled
Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person, injuring more than 500, and uprooting trees and severing power as it weakened and ⁠headed north toward ⁠the ​Chinese coast.
Earlier classified as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the ⁠Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of about 126km per hour (78 miles per hour) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat Marina Dunbar and Fran Lawther
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

With less than two weeks until the midterms, my colleague Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US columnist Moira Donegan are answering your questions in this week’s episode of Politics Weekly America.
They break down the final stretch ahead of these hugely consequential elections, that will decide control of Congress in Donald Trump’s final two years of office.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ramaswamy accuses Acton of ‘lying’ about attack ad, but court records contradict mother’s claim – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Letters from federal prosecutors represent latest escalation as Trump continues to make claims of voter fraud
Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on Friday demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Department of Justice said may belong to noncitizens, according to the Los Angeles county registrar and a letter obtained by the Associated Press.
The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and Donald Trump’s Department of Justice, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California officials ordered by DoJ to set aside ‘likely’ noncitizen ballots

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Footage broadcast on state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots
Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180km (110 miles) south of the capital, Amman.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seven killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Defense secretary Pete Hegseth alleges Confucius Institutes operating in disguise on US university campuses
The ⁠US defense department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centers on university campuses ⁠known as Confucius ⁠Institutes ​as a threat to US national security, defense secretary Pete ⁠Hegseth said on Friday.
Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda ⁠tools and has taken steps to ​crack down on them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon designates China-backed campus cultural centers a threat to US national security

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
WA politician says he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be ‘unacceptable’

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator releases a letter detailing the allegations against him.
After days of confusion following historical complaints about alleged misconduct were publicly aired in the media, Steele-John posted a statement to social media late Friday night.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public

articles.author: Adeshola Ore
articles.description:
Independent MP now serious but stable, according to update from Melbourne’s Alfred hospital

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Independent MP Helen Haines’s condition has been downgraded to serious but stable after she lost both legs following an alleged attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria on Monday afternoon.
The Alfred hospital in Melbourne provided an update on Haines’s condition on Saturday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Helen Haines’s condition improves days after losing both legs from alleged attack

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from Iran
Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.
The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio tells Cubans ‘now is the time’ to act to see political change

articles.author: Adeshola Ore with Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Parts of Queensland, Victoria and South Australia can expect severe storms on Saturday, moving into NSW and Tasmania by Sunday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Severe thunderstorms and heavy rain will sweep across most Australian states this weekend, adding to the deluge in an already drenched Queensland.
Flash flooding in south-east Queensland this week prompted hundreds of SES callouts and the closure of multiple schools. On Saturday morning, the Bureau of Meteorology had nine flood warnings in place for south Queensland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and flash flooding predicted for much of Australia

articles.author: Dani Anguiano
articles.description:
Kaylub Giamanco recounts the day he confronted the Silver Rail elementary school shooter, who killed three boys and one teacher
The Oregon father hailed as a hero for stopping a school shooting last week spoke for the first time about the incident, describing his experience and how he told a 911 operator: “I have to go in. People are going to die.”
Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, has received national attention and praise for stopping the bloodshed at Silver Rail elementary in Bend, Oregon, where his children attend school.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Father who killed Oregon school shooter speaks out for first time: ‘I have to go in’

articles.author: Tara Conlan
articles.description:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say
The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said.
Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Campaigners call lack of progress ‘staggering’ as online regulator issues review of first nine months of new regime
Landmark online safety measures have failed to limit the proportion of children suffering harm from social media, the UK’s online regulator has admitted, in an assessment branded “staggering” by campaigners.
The proportion of children being fed unsafe content that often left them frightened, confused and upset, was almost unchanged, according to an Ofcom review of the first nine months of supposedly strict requirements on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Online safety laws have failed to protect children in UK, Ofcom admits

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
David Shoebridge’s newly-minted leadership under pressure over handling of misconduct allegations as Senate estimates looms

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

More than a week after allegations that Greens senator Jordon Steele-John had behaved inappropriately towards women made headlines, his position in the party remains in limbo and its new leader’s handling of the issue in question.
David Shoebridge’s first major challenge at the helm of the federal Greens came earlier this month when the Nine newspapers reported a three-page letter had been sent to him urging an independent investigation into Steele-John.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jordon Steele-John’s position remains in limbo as Greens prepare for moment in spotlight

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Yassin El-Moudden
articles.description:
Dozens of schools in Cornwall also affected as Storm Boelo heads for Scotland, Northern Ireland and north of England
Thousands of homes are without power and schools were closed as the first named storm of the year hit UK shores.
Storm Austen brought severe conditions to parts of the south-west, with a gust of 76mph recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly on Friday morning. By 3pm, more than 31,000 homes in the south-west were without power, according to National Grid.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands of homes without power as Storm Austen hits south-west England

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Gunman opens fire from car in Trappes and Verrière, killing one and injuring five others, including a 12-year-old girl
Emmanuel Macron has condemned racism in French society after a gunman opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person, wounding a 12-year-old girl and injuring four others in what the president called a “racist terrorist attack”.
Macron arrived at the scene of the drive-by shooting in Trappes on Friday night, saying he was deeply saddened by what he called the “premeditated” attack. The 12-year-old girl, who was shot eight times, is being treated in hospital.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron condemns racism after one killed in ‘terrorist’ shooting near Paris

articles.author: Yassin El-Moudden, Lucy Campbell, Frances Mao and Martin Belam
articles.description:
Residents in Oleshky have been enduring a worsening humanitarian crisis due to the lack of food, electricity and other resources 
The French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu has just issued a statement on a shooting in a town west of Paris this morning where one person was killed and four others injured.
Police said a gunman had opened fire in Trappes, in the Yvelines, and neighbouring La Verriere. The gunman was later arrested in nearby Coignieres.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Melania Trump has helped broker ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town, says White House – as it happened

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Houses being targeted because they are thought to hold immigrants, with dozens of properties affected in recent weeks
Criminals are recruiting vulnerable people, including children, to damage houses suspected of being HMOs, police in Manchester believe.
In recent weeks, dozens of properties have been targeted across Greater Manchester, mostly in Salford, but also in Stockport and Tameside.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Criminals recruiting children to damage Greater Manchester HMOs, police believe

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Benjamin Netanyahu and ministers promise demolitions and forced displacement after deadly gunfight
Israel has launched a campaign of collective punishment against Palestinians in Hebron after gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and injured three near a checkpoint outside the city.
Benjamin Netanyahu announced a siege on Hebron and neighbouring Halhul and said residents of the gunmen’s home neighbourhoods would all be forced out. He promised mass demolitions of homes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel launches collective punishment campaign in Hebron after two soldiers killed

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Multinational ‘anti-war bloc’ uses Istanbul summit to call for a diplomatic solution to Middle East crisis
Foreign ministers at a summit of eight European and Middle Eastern countries have urged the US and Israel not to renews their attacks on Iran, warning a fresh outbreak of fighting would spread conflict and push oil prices even higher.
The development of a new multinational “anti-war bloc” represents a challenge to the increasingly open plans by the US and Israel to relaunch strikes on Iran while talks on Tehran’s nuclear programme remain deadlocked.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US and Israel are warned against launching fresh strikes on Iran

articles.author: Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Prosecution says Robinson guilty of harassment of Daily Mail journalists because we do not live in a ‘vigilante world’ 
Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a “vigilante world”, jurors have been told, as the prosecution sought to use the far-right activist’s words against him.
Robinson had posted a video in which he told Daily Mail journalists he would find them after they wrote about his alleged role influencing England’s 2024 riots. He told them he had obtained details of where they and their families lived and warned them to abide by “men’s rules”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tommy Robinson ‘threatened people and acted like a bully’, jury told

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Duchess of Sussex ‘deeply distressed’ over child sexual abuse image claims against father

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Brent crude increase follows Tehran threatening retaliatory attacks on Gulf refineries and datacentres
Oil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil price rises above $117 a barrel amid fears US will renew strikes on Iran

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
articles.description:
Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing
A political ad from Spain’s main opposition party that used a deepfake video of the prime minister’s wife has sparked outrage and set off a wider debate on AI, as the deeply polarised country gears up for general elections next month.
Launched this week across the social media channels of the conservative People’s party (PP), the video used artificial intelligence to manipulate the likenesses of various people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party and appeared to show them admitting to acts such as soliciting prostitutes and taking kickbacks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Opposition deepfake video sparks outrage in Spain ahead of election

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer and Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
People in Russian-occupied city facing severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with some reportedly surviving on weeds
The White House has said that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where a deepening humanitarian crisis has left thousands of civilians struggling to survive.
In a statement on Friday, the White House said both sides had agreed to halt all military operations in the city from 27 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for the evacuation of civilians.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to local ceasefire in Oleshky amid deepening humanitarian crisis

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Search and rescue efforts under way after quake strikes region’s north, with at least seven aftershocks recorded
A magnitude-7 earthquake has hit Tibet, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and destroying hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media have said.
Search and rescue efforts continued after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, according to China’s national broadcaster CCTV.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes

articles.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
articles.description:
Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed
The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.
From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’

articles.author: Patrick Commins
articles.description:
High inflation, low growth and rising unemployment can be added to the federal treasurer’s wall of worries

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Jim Chalmers in a speech last week offered the scant encouragement that the economy would be “a bit better” in a year’s time.
Fast forward to Friday morning, and the treasurer revealed that his officials were busy downgrading their forecasts ahead of December’s mid-year budget update to show slower growth and higher unemployment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jim Chalmers faces a world of hard choices where the solution to one problem makes the other worse

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Tom Phillips; produced by Ivor Manley, Eli Block and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips, heads to Roraima to hear what’s at stake for the rainforest and the communities that live there in the Brazilian presidential runoff on Sunday. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com
For the Amazon and the communities who live there, the stakes in Sunday’s Brazilian presidential election runoff could scarcely be higher.
Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips heads to Roraima, the country’s most northern state, to hear from voters, preachers and politicians in a region that heavily backed Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil’s election and the battle for the Amazon – podcast

articles.author: Giles Richards in Austin
articles.description:
41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’

Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record

Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.
Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Sasan Ghandehari’s partnership with religious foundation raises questions about past dealings with republic criticised by Nigel Farage
Nigel Farage’s newest billionaire donor was in business with a powerful Iranian religious foundation under the authority of the country’s supreme leader, raising questions about his past dealings with the hardline republic.
Hossein Ghandehari, also called Sasan, was little known in the UK until he pledged to give millions to Reform UK this summer and donated £50,000 to Farage to cover the cost of two passes for the Davos World Economic Forum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: billionaire Reform donor was in business with foundation linked to Iranian regime

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
‘Scapegoating non-permanent residents is not going to lower the cost of living,’ Vanesa Ortiz says
When Vanesa Ortiz came to Calgary from Mexico, she found herself in a city gripped by winter. Outside the airport, it was -15C (5F).
“I would come to understand that this was not an extreme cold,” she said. “But in the moment it was terrifying.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alberta welcomed migrant workers. Now, it wants to restrict their rights

articles.author: Jonathan Yerushalmy and agencies
articles.description:
Similar withdrawals from UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain reported as concerns grow about restart of war on Iran after US midterm elections
The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia as the gulf kingdom faces a barrage of near-daily attacks, with at least three people killed at an airport and oilfield.
Attacks on “civilian airports and other critical infrastructure” by the Iranian-supported Houthis in Yemen were highlighted as the reason for the drawdown. The state department spokesperson, Tommy Pigott, said: “The safety and security of department personnel and their families remain our highest priority.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Some US diplomats told to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Yangon
articles.description:
Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son speaks to detained former Myanmar leader for first time in five years

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, issues warning after inspecting border fortifications against backdrop of rising tensions
Propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border, Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has said amid a worsening of ties between the two countries.
The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, came a day after she said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: North Korea prepares to restart propaganda loudspeakers as ties sour with South

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’
The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.
It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors say
Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping.
Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has vowed to take by force if necessary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown
An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.
The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.
Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity
Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.
With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird
A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel.
Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.
Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall.
That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home

articles.author: David Smith in Austin, Texas
articles.description:
The Senate candidate denounced opponent Ken Paxton, calling out corruption allegations and support from Musk
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Texas, has taken aim at Elon Musk, warning that the tech mogul is trying to buy political influence and declaring: “Texas is not for sale.”
Talarico held a campaign rally on Friday at the University of Texas at Austin, packing an auditorium at his alma mater with hundreds of students and other supporters, who cheered, whooped and waved campaign signs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat James Talarico targets Elon Musk at rally: ‘Texas is not for sale’

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat Marina Dunbar and Fran Lawther
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

With less than two weeks until the midterms, my colleague Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US columnist Moira Donegan are answering your questions in this week’s episode of Politics Weekly America.
They break down the final stretch ahead of these hugely consequential elections, that will decide control of Congress in Donald Trump’s final two years of office.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ramaswamy accuses Acton of ‘lying’ about attack ad, but court records contradict mother’s claim – as it happened

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from Iran
Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.
The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio tells Cubans ‘now is the time’ to act to see political change

articles.author: Shrai Popat and Lucy Campbell
articles.description:
With just 11 days until the US midterm elections, Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reclaim Congress
With just 11 days until the US midterm elections, early voting data is rolling in nationwide. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reclaim the majority in each chamber of Congress. Here is where the numbers stand as of Friday:
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Surging turnout, with Democrats voting more: key takeaways from early voting data

articles.author: Gaya Gupta in New York
articles.description:
Republican senator faces critical re-election battle in state where president’s trade war has outraged voters 
Donald Trump dropped some of the US’s tariffs on Canada on Friday to “better serve the public interest” the White House said, handing a win to Susan Collins, the embattled Republican senator for Maine, as she faces a tight re-election campaign that will help determine whether Democrats can flip control of Congress.
Collins announced that the exemptions would apply to nine agricultural products, including blueberries, potatoes, apples and seaweed. She added that many of the state’s farmers rely on specialized equipment and materials from across the border that are “unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump drops some Canada tariffs in bid to boost embattled Susan Collins in Maine

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Donald Trump told rally-goers on Thursday evening that he had 'the right to run again' for president, invoking a claim he has repeatedly made that he may seek a third term despite it being unconstitutional
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump floats unconstitutional third term at campaign rally in Iowa – video

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
Republicans are resorting to childish taunts to defend an uncommonly dishonorable state attorney general
It’s a bit like Lucy with the football. Every few years, Democrats convince themselves that a Texas Senate seat might finally switch from red to blue. On paper, it makes sense. Texas is a large and urbanizing state with an increasingly educated – and increasingly non-white – population.
Other one-time Republican strongholds that have undergone similar demographic shifts have turned purple or even blueish – think Georgia, for example. The border counties along the Rio Grande valley, with their deep poverty and big Latino populations, were long thought to be fertile ground to nurture a kind of anti-Trump populism that could be converted into pro-Democratic sentiment. The state Democratic party is anemic there, but a few talented candidates have emerged.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A Democratic win in Texas is a long shot – but Ken Paxton’s weakness is obvious | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
Byron Donalds removed mentions of the president from his website and has barely uttered his name – will his ploy prove successful in a tight governor’s race?
It took Byron Donalds, addressing a wildly supportive crowd at a rally in Florida’s bluest county, some time to list those he blamed for any “affordability” issues they might be experiencing.
Joe Biden, and the radical policies of the Democrats, were at fault, the Republican nominee for Florida governor insisted in his stump speech at Broward county’s Green Glades West ranch, even though neither has wielded power in Washington for almost two years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Maga governor candidate in the Maga state who is not talking about Trump

articles.author: Sidney Blumenthal
articles.description:
The US president is portraying Zelenskyy as the villain as he strives for Russia’s approval
If Donald Trump could, he would fly to Munich to sign away Ukraine to Vladimir Putin, and return to wave the document as “peace in our time”, hoping to claim at least the second Fifa peace prize.
Whatever the complicated motives of Neville Chamberlain, his well-grounded fear after the carnage of a world war of another apocalypse and his wishful thinking that Hitler would be satiated after carving up Czechoslovakia, Chamberlain had not sent his son-in-law and former golf partner and real estate partner in advance to cut back-end deals with the Nazis to profit for his family and cronies.
Sidney Blumenthal, former senior adviser to Bill Clinton and Hillary Clinton, has published three books of a projected five-volume political life of Abraham Lincoln: A Self-Made Man, Wrestling With His Angel and All the Powers of Earth. He is a Guardian US columnist and co-host of the Court of History podcast
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Trump-Putin love story’s next chapter: selling out Ukraine | Sidney Blumenthal

articles.author: Nick Romeo
articles.description:
An old idea springs anew as a chorus of influential voices predicts that AI may trigger crises of vast magnitude
In a preface to his book Capitalism and Freedom, the American economist Milton Friedman famously observed that a crisis can propel once-fringe ideas into the political mainstream.
“Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is a job guarantee the solution to mass AI unemployment?

articles.author: Shrai Popat, Hazel Tang, John Farrell, Karif Wat
articles.description:
To reclaim control of the Senate, Democrats need to retain all the Senate seats they have and flip four more in the 2026 midterm elections.  Shrai Popat, the Guardian's US politics reporter, explains which are the key races to watch in November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: These key races in the 2026 midterms will decide who controls the US Senate – video explainer

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
The president shows a unique disregard for the opinions, norms and ideals of the nation – and, for that matter, humanity
The Democrats’ focus on affordability seems to be a winning strategy (we’ll know for sure in a little over two weeks). But we mustn’t lose sight of the moral squalor at the core of the Trump regime and the necessity of ending it.
It’s that moral squalor – the utter disregard for the opinions, norms and ideals of the nation and, for that matter, of humanity – that uniquely marks Trump and the reprobates he has attracted to Washington. It has also poisoned much of the Republican party, including the billionaires and tech bros who finance it.
Robert Reich, a former US secretary of labor, is a professor of public policy emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley. He is a Guardian US columnist and his newsletter is at robertreich.substack.com. His new book, Coming Up Short: A Memoir of My America, is out now in the US and in the UK
 Continue reading...
articles.title: America must reverse Trump’s moral squalor | Robert Reich

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
The current US administration is an obstacle, but public demand for protection will ultimately prevail
Organisations around the world scrambled on Thursday to fix critical flaws in PHP, the software that powers much of the web. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take control of affected servers. Some websites were taken offline as a precaution while fixes were installed. The paradox is that while AI helped researchers uncover the flaw, it also threatens to accelerate the ability to exploit it. Amazon said that it had detected an attempt before the public disclosure of the PHP flaws.
What the episode highlights is AI’s central role in security – and not always for the right reasons. OpenAI’s models have also been responsible for two alarming hacks this year – a security breach of an Australian health department website and a raid by a swarm of AI bots on Hugging Face, an AI services platform. Citing those incidents, the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, warned that a similar cyber-attack on the UK is “likely, if not inevitable”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on AI safety: the push for global regulation must advance | Editorial

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
Datacenters, AI and distaste for the billionaires developing it has soured Americans on big tech

How will Trump’s mass deportation agenda shape the US midterm elections? Our reporters answer your questions

The campaign ad begins with a clear, idyllic stream that suddenly turns sludge-brown as two concrete datacenters slam on to its banks. Another facility thuds down on a peaceful suburban park, and two more crush-green pastures as an ominous soundtrack to a disaster movie blares.
“They’re coming for our rivers. Our neighborhoods. Our farmland,” a deep-voiced narrator says. “Because Brent Taylor wrote the law allowing datacenters to take over Tennessee.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How tech became the villain of the US midterms

articles.author: Debbie Carlson in Chicago, Chris Stein in Ohio and Sam Levine in Missouri
articles.description:
Polls show US voters are deeply upset by high gas prices and are likely to punish Republicans in the midterms as a result

How will Trump’s mass deportation agenda shape the US midterm elections? Our reporters answer your questions

With fewer than two weeks until the midterms, US voters are unlikely to see relief on one of this election cycle’s main issues: gas prices.
Airing up her car’s tires at a Speedway in Perrysburg, Ohio, Toledo resident Sharie Smith, 41, says soaring costs are having a direct impact on her life.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Too little, too late: Trump takes on gas prices as fuel costs hamper his midterm hopes

articles.author: Oliver Laughland, Tom Silverstone, Katie Lamborn, Jem Talbot, Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
A battle for Alabama’s second congressional district is being fought against a backdrop of partisan gerrymandering and America’s ongoing civil rights struggle. Oliver Laughland and Tom Silverstone track down the Maga Republican Rhett Marques who is looking to unseat Democratic incumbent Shomari Figures but won’t answer questions about redistricting. Meanwhile, lower-income residents in rural parts of the district are still fighting for basic sanitation rights after Donald Trump ended federal assistance, which the administration described as 'illegal DEI'.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Alabama's Republicans are disenfranchising Black voters – video

articles.author: Hosted by Carter Sherman and Kai Wright with Sam Levine and George Chidi . Produced by Monica Espitia, engineered by Ivan Kuraev, executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
This week, the Department of Justice charged 28 green card holders in California over alleged voter fraud. It’s the latest move by the Trump administration to crack down on noncitizen voters, and part of a wider push to throw the results of the midterms into doubt. In today's episode, Carter Sherman and Kai Wright are joined by George Chidi and Sam Levine, two reporters who have spent years covering Donald Trump’s attacks on voting rights. They analyze the tactics being used to purge voter rolls, and look ahead to how Trump might react if the results on election day don’t go his way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump going to steal the midterms? - Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Tara Conlan
articles.description:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say
The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said.
Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Campaigners call lack of progress ‘staggering’ as online regulator issues review of first nine months of new regime
Landmark online safety measures have failed to limit the proportion of children suffering harm from social media, the UK’s online regulator has admitted, in an assessment branded “staggering” by campaigners.
The proportion of children being fed unsafe content that often left them frightened, confused and upset, was almost unchanged, according to an Ofcom review of the first nine months of supposedly strict requirements on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Online safety laws have failed to protect children in UK, Ofcom admits

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Yassin El-Moudden
articles.description:
Dozens of schools in Cornwall also affected as Storm Boelo heads for Scotland, Northern Ireland and north of England
Thousands of homes are without power and schools were closed as the first named storm of the year hit UK shores.
Storm Austen brought severe conditions to parts of the south-west, with a gust of 76mph recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly on Friday morning. By 3pm, more than 31,000 homes in the south-west were without power, according to National Grid.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands of homes without power as Storm Austen hits south-west England

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Houses being targeted because they are thought to hold immigrants, with dozens of properties affected in recent weeks
Criminals are recruiting vulnerable people, including children, to damage houses suspected of being HMOs, police in Manchester believe.
In recent weeks, dozens of properties have been targeted across Greater Manchester, mostly in Salford, but also in Stockport and Tameside.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Criminals recruiting children to damage Greater Manchester HMOs, police believe

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Government’s emergency planning advice has sparked sales of essentials but no panic stockpiling, say prepping shop owners
When the UK government launched its “Protect and Survive” public information campaign in 1980 on how to stay alive after a nuclear attack, it was met with a combination of scepticism, disbelief and derision.
The advice included how to build a “fallout room” at home, how to whitewash windows to protect from a blast, and how to store a dead body for up to five days.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Realistic and reassuring’: UK public ‘responding calmly’ to Be Ready campaign

articles.author: Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Prosecution says Robinson guilty of harassment of Daily Mail journalists because we do not live in a ‘vigilante world’ 
Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a “vigilante world”, jurors have been told, as the prosecution sought to use the far-right activist’s words against him.
Robinson had posted a video in which he told Daily Mail journalists he would find them after they wrote about his alleged role influencing England’s 2024 riots. He told them he had obtained details of where they and their families lived and warned them to abide by “men’s rules”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tommy Robinson ‘threatened people and acted like a bully’, jury told

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Duchess of Sussex ‘deeply distressed’ over child sexual abuse image claims against father

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Party insiders say they expect initial verdict to be against leader and are preparing to appeal against adverse findings
Nigel Farage’s Reform is braced for a negative report from the standards commissioner over his failure to declare a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne and plans to appeal against any adverse findings.
The party is on tenterhooks over the report, with multiple Reform insiders saying they are readying for a fightback through the appeals process and fully expect the initial verdict to find against their leader.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK braces for Farage standards verdict over undeclared £5m gift

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Historic England archaeologist says some inns’ claims to date back 1,000 years are inaccurate and oldest is from 1430
With their low ceilings, timber beams and roaring fires, many of England’s inns lay claim to being the oldest in the land and to have been visited by Vikings and Saxons.
But an archaeologist who worked on behalf of Historic England says not one of the more than two dozen pubs that make this claim is being accurate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Which is really England’s oldest pub? Tree-ring dating helps settle debate

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Duchess of Sussex’s decision to cut ties with elderly father cast in new light as he faces sexual abuse image claims

Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by allegations against father

The depiction of the Duchess of Sussex by certain sections of the media has often been one of a fame-hungry daughter casting off an elderly father in his declining years and keeping him from his grandchildren as she embraces the international celebrity stage.
Their estrangement has been the subject of countless headlines since her marriage to Prince Harry. But her statement today, released after child sexual abuse image allegations made against Thomas Markle Sr, 82, suggests deeper, darker fears as the cause.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Allegations against Thomas Markle Sr challenge media’s Meghan narrative

articles.author: Aisha Down
articles.description:
Exclusive: Key figure in campaign group accused of saying she would ‘never hire a black person’, and second figure discussed Sydney Sweeney’s ‘assets’
The Free Speech Union (FSU) is reeling from internal grievances involving allegations of racism, workplace discrimination and sexually inappropriate remarks by senior members of staff, the Guardian can reveal.
A key figure in the campaign group, the chief operating officer, Sigrun Olafsdottir, departed late last week after employees alleged that she told a junior member of staff she would “never hire a black person” as a part of a one-on-one meeting late last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Free Speech Union hit by internal allegations of racism and sexually inappropriate remarks

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham join William on sofa for special edition to celebrate prince’s Earthshot prize
The Prince of Wales has braved the chatshow sofa, making a surprise appearance on The Graham Norton Show.
In the pre-recorded show, to be aired on Friday on BBC One, William made a surprise appearance in a special Earthshot prize edition to promote his environmental initiative, which has an annual awards ceremony due to be staged in Mumbai, India, next month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prince William makes surprise appearance on Graham Norton show

articles.author: Harry Taylor (now and earlier) and Martin Belam (earlier)
articles.description:
The prime minister said the government is having conversation about emergency preparedness
A DUP minister has said he is confident MP Carla Lockhart will stay in the party despite leaving its main decision-making body amid a row with party leadership over the future of Stormont.
Lockhart is at odds with DUP leader, fellow MP Gavin Robinson, over whether the party should withdraw deputy first minister Emma Little-Pengelly from the power-sharing executive.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Andy Burnham warns of ‘winter of greater flooding’ – as it happened

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Angela Eagle tells utility bosses next price review ‘must focus on value for money for customers’
Ministers will make an unprecedented intervention in water bills and how companies prioritise investment, directing bosses to bring down costs and stop leaks and sewage overflows.
Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, has told suppliers in England and Wales she plans to intervene in the next price review – conducted by the water regulator, Ofwat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government to make unprecedented intervention in setting of water bills

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM’s revelation follows launch of advice for households to have enough water and food to get by in civil emergency
Andy Burnham has said he has stockpiles of beans, soup and Twiglets in case of a civil emergency, as he said a new government campaign was not a reason for panic buying.
The prime minister was questioned on his domestic supply situation after the Be Ready campaign advised households to have enough bottled water and long-life food to keep going in case of an emergency, such as one caused by a weather event or a cyber-attack.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham says he has emergency stockpile of beans, soup and Twiglets

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
New PM has prioritised small fixes to show voters Labour can make a real difference, and government insiders are delighted at the public’s reaction
In the first episode of Armando Iannucci’s political satire The Thick of It, the hapless minister Hugh Abbot is in the back of a taxi, frantically brainstorming for an on-the-hoof policy he can announce to the assembled national press.
“So you want something sexy and eye-catching, and that is free and universally popular and instantly applicable. No one can possibly object to it,” says the addled junior adviser Ollie Reeder. “Well, really, you should have said something before then, because I’ve got a file about that fucking thick of that back in the office.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Potholes, bus fares and headphone dodgers: will Burnham’s strategy of ‘everyday fixes’ succeed?

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Latest negative economic update comes as John Healey prepares to announce budget next week
Retail sales in Great Britain fell more steeply than expected last month, the latest negative economic update before the chancellor, John Healey, announces his budget next week.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the volume of goods sold fell 0.4% month on month in September, much steeper than economists’ consensus expectations of a 0.1% fall.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Retail sales in Great Britain fall as struggling households cut back

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
World’s second largest brewer says use of drugs such as Wegovy can reduce desire to drink alcohol
Heineken has warned British bars and pubs that the boom in popularity of weight-loss drugs could lead to a fall in sales of beer and cider.
The world’s second-largest brewer sent a presentation to British hospitality customers earlier this month that said the use of GLP-1 medication – such as Ozempic and Wegovy – could reduce the desire to drink alcohol. This in turn could result in “fullness and fewer serves” of pints in pubs and bars, it added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boom in weight-loss drugs could lead to fall in beer sales, Heineken warns UK pubs

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Photographer Simon Montgomery told ‘state’s interest in regulated immigration’ outweighs his family concerns
A British photographer is facing deportation from Sweden and forced separation from his 16-month-old son after authorities ruled in favour of the country’s immigration interests.
Simon Montgomery’s application to remain after the birth of his son last year was rejected on several grounds by Sweden’s migration agency, a decision that was then upheld by the migration court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Briton facing forced separation from baby son after Sweden orders his deportation

articles.author: Megan Davies, Claire Jones and Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm Adam brings torrential rain to Valencia, Alicante and Balearic Islands, as Storm Austen strikes England and Wales
Storm Adam brought torrential rain to eastern Spain earlier this week. In Pego, Alicante, 632mm fell in 36 hours, with 430mm of this falling in just six hours, while the Valencian town of Olivia received 600mm in 24 hours.
The severe flooding led 145 municipalities across Valencia and Alicante to impose a temporary lockdown on about 850,000 people on Monday. At least five people have died, 500 have been rescued and 2,100 evacuated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Severe flooding in eastern Spain and UK hit by first named storm of winter

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Economic fallout from war in Middle East adds to pressures on consumers and on chancellor before budget
Consumer confidence in the UK has fallen at the fastest rate outside the Covid pandemic since the 2016 Brexit vote as the escalating economic damage from the war in the Middle East hits Britain.
With less than a week before John Healey’s first budget, the latest barometer from the data company GfK indicated confidence plunged by 11 percentage points in October to -24 amid pressure on consumers from the rising cost of living.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK consumer confidence falls at fastest rate since Brexit vote as cost of living bites

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Officials will call on UK to ‘step up’ financial support at Brussels summit – with post-Brexit issues also on agenda
EU leaders will press Andy Burnham at a summit in Brussels to contribute more to Ukraine’s defence effort in 2027.
EU officials argue that the UK, Canada and Japan should do more to support Ukraine, but entreaties to these G7 countries for extra financial aid at recent international meetings have not been answered, Brussels says.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU leaders to press Burnham to pay more towards Ukraine’s defence

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Official forecasts show country will meet energy demand by paying high prices to secure imports
Great Britain is expected to pay some of the highest energy costs in Europe this winter as its reliance on imports to ensure a steady supply is forecast to deepen.
Energy system operators have said the country will have enough gas and electricity to meet demand over the coldest months – in part because of paying higher market prices than neighbouring markets to secure imports.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Some of Europe’s highest energy costs expected in Britain this winter

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
People succumbed to heat at highest rates in Malta, Italy and Hungary, with health issues, loneliness and poverty exacerbating toll
Heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities this summer, new research suggests, with scientists blaming climate breakdown for two in every three of the deaths.
Morgues and funeral homes filled with bodies from June to August as the heat added by planet-baking pollution cut short an extra 32,000 lives in urban areas, the researchers found. Hot days pushed vulnerable bodies into overdrive and warm nights prevented them from recovering.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Heat killed ‘staggering’ 50,000 people in Europe’s cities this summer, scientists warn

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
CQC research finds long delays are making  conditions harder to treat and highlights regional disparities in care
Thousands of children in England are experiencing some of the sharpest rises in waiting times for healthcare in the history of the NHS, a report has revealed.
While some adult waiting times have improved, children and young people are being “hit hardest” amid soaring demand and falling numbers of staff, according to the annual state of care report by the Care Quality Commission.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Child health in England at risk from sharp rise in NHS waiting times, report says

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
PM will also announce funding for specialised protective gear and the deployment of military aircraft

The UK government is to create an AI Cobra unit to spot wildfires after this year’s record-breaking summer saw devastating blazes across the country.
The country experienced its hottest-ever summer this year, with prolonged dry periods and extreme heat fuelling wildfires that triggered an emergency alert to mobile phones in England and Wales. Figures released on 8 October showed a clear upward trend in the number of fires recorded each year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to reveal plans for AI unit to tackle wildfires after scorching summer

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas Music editor
articles.description:
Singer who has had record-breaking Brit awards success adds to haul thanks to massively ambitious big-band album
Raye is the winner of the 2026 Mercury prize, for her second studio album, This Music May Contain Hope.
Her win – for a hugely ambitious 73-minute record that spanned big band jazz, power balladry, funk and more – caps an ongoing renaissance for a British singer who at one point was in the doldrums, lashing out publicly at her record label for not letting her release a studio album.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Raye wins 2026 Mercury prize for This Music May Contain Hope

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Regulators say removing ‘unnecessary burdens’ will save businesses about £2bn over 10 years
The UK is watering down rules introduced in the aftermath of the financial crisis that were designed to hold City bosses accountable for wrongdoing.
The plans, put forward by the financial industry’s two top regulators, the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), include a reduction in reporting for “lower-level misconduct” and would also free 140,000 managers from extra checks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to relax post-2008 rules that hold City bosses accountable for wrongdoing

articles.author: Owen Myers
articles.description:
Stage show based on late singer reportedly set to feature her best-loved songs with involvement from her father Mitch
A musical based on Amy Winehouse is in development for London’s West End.
The project is still in early stages with Catherine Schreiber, a Tony award-winning producer (Cabaret, Rent), attached to the project, according to Variety. Casting is reported to currently be under way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Amy Winehouse musical in development for West End

articles.author: Eben Muse
articles.description:
People near south Wales river were told to keep windows and doors shut after thousands of litres of kerosene from a GE Aerospace site got into the water
Oily slicks of kerosene still appeared to be leaking into the River Taff this week, several days after a breach of thousands of litres was spotted by members of the public.
The breach into the Welsh river was identified last Friday, after people reported strong chemical odours emanating from it. Natural Resources Wales (NRW) officers arrived on site soon afterwards to identify the source of the pollution and were assisted by the south Wales fire and rescue service, which placed absorbent mats and booms to contain as much kerosene as possible.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Unsafe water, burning eyes and kerosene slicks: residents demand answers on River Taff leak

articles.author: Presented by Jessica Elgot and Alexandra Topping, produced by Danielle Stephens, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
The government has given the go-ahead for the Jackdaw gasfield, but that was the easy part. The next big headache is the Rosebank oilfield. The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, has indicated she might reject this licence because of the project’s expected environmental impact, but could Andy Burnham overrule her to help the chancellor, John Healey?
You can read Kiran Stacey’s exclusive report on Rosebank here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rosebank row: will Labour block the oilfield? – podcast

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Fears over lack of scrutiny for key sectors as health editor position also to go in cuts aimed at saving £5.5m
The BBC will no longer have a dedicated education editor as part of a cost-cutting drive in which 100 jobs are to go across BBC News under a plan that school leaders described as “deeply regrettable”.
BBC staff have been told that the roles of education editor and social affairs editor are to be combined into a single position as part of a round of changes that will save £5.5m. However, prominent unions and campaigners are saying the reform will dilute scrutiny of two specialisms that are too important to go without a dedicated BBC role.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BBC News to axe education editor role in cost-cutting move

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Aletha Adu; produced by Saskia Collette, Eli Block, Claudia Efemini and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Political correspondent Aletha Adu explores whether the Conservative party under Kemi Badenoch is about to become, once again, the UK’s leading party on the right. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com
What makes Kemi Badenoch one of the most popular party leaders in the UK? And can she drag the Tory party back with her?
For two years, the momentum on the British right has been only with one party – Nigel Farage’s Reform UK. But recently, something has begun to change. Polls currently have the Conservatives and Reform neck-and-neck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are the Tories back? - podcast

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
Relatives recount distress and loneliness their loved ones went through in pandemic as a result of isolation policy
“At the time it felt like a devil’s bargain – it was horrible, but it was what [we thought] we had to do to keep people safe,” says Amy of the “devastating” and “terrifying” restrictions that led to her maternal grandparents being locked down in separate care homes during the early days of the Covid-19 pandemic.
Eva and Eric had been married for more than 60 years when her dementia and his increased frailty meant they needed separate residential support. When the first lockdown was announced in March 2020, however, it in effect cut them off from each other and their granddaughter, to whom they had been especially close after the early death of Amy’s mother.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It should never be forgotten’: families recount care home victims’ experiences in wake of Covid findings

articles.author: Kiran Stacey, Jessica Elgot and Fiona Harvey
articles.description:
Exclusive: Officials say Miatta Fahnbulleh minded not to give approval in victory for climate campaigners

Miatta Fahnbulleh is minded to reject the giant Rosebank oilfield, sources have told the Guardian, in what would be a blow for the North Sea energy industry and a major victory for climate campaigners.
After approving the smaller Jackdaw gasfield on Wednesday, officials say the energy secretary is leaning towards refusing approval for what would be one of the biggest oilfields in the North Sea.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy secretary leaning towards rejecting Rosebank oilfield

articles.description:
The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, thanked the prime minister for backing Jackdaw after the Tories approved it in 2022. But Burnham said he made a decision on something the Tories messed up, and the government had made a bridge to the future and the transition to clean energy


UK politics live – latest updates

UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea

Climate campaigners condemn ‘maddening’ decision to approve Jackdaw gasfield

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham says decision on Jackdaw is something the Tories 'messed up' - video

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
A look at some of the options after PM is urged to consider radical alternatives to deal with stricken company
Andy Burnham has told officials to rip up their plans for how to fix Thames Water and present him with more radical options for what to do with the stricken company. Here are some ideas the prime minister is being urged to consider.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How might Andy Burnham tackle Thames Water debacle?

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Decision has implications for household energy bills, the UK economy and the climate crisis

UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea

Nils Pratley: Jackdaw approval is a step towards a grownup North Sea policy


About four years and six energy secretaries after it was given the green light, the Jackdaw gasfield has been given consent to begin production 150 miles east of Aberdeen.
So what does this long-awaited decision mean for the Labour party, household bills, the economy and the climate crisis?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What does the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?

articles.author: Aisha Down
articles.description:
Our dependence on internet services of a few key tech companies leaves us vulnerable to cloud failures, bugs and more, experts say
It happened again. A power outage hit a datacentre in London, and things cascaded from there: multiple banking services faltered, court hearings were put on hold and patients reported temporary glitches on the NHS app.
The datacentre in question was in Google’s europe-west2-b zone, one of more than a dozen “zones” that the US search giant maintains in Europe to service its clients.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Too big to not fail’: Google outage exposes UK reliance on a handful of cloud providers

articles.description:
Amateur wildlife photographer Rhys Morgan has caught extraordinary footage of one of the largest whale species on Earth. 

While sailing off the Pembrokeshire coast in Wales, Morgan and his friends spotted the blowholes of a fin whale in the distance, recognisable by the hooked fin near its tail, a dark grey upper body, white belly, and an asymmetrical jaw that is dark on the left and white on the right.

People who have enjoyed the video online are trying to raise awareness of fin whales being hunted in Iceland and calling on government ministers to take action
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Whale in Wales: amateur photographer captures stunning footage - video

articles.author: Presented by Ian Sample, produced by Madeleine Finlay, sound design by Ross Burns, the executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
In his annual speech on threats to the nation, Sir Ken McCallum, the head of the UK’s intelligence service, MI5, warned that AI had the potential to ‘change the stakes’ on existing and even new bioweapons. To find out why, and how, Ian Sample speaks to Dr Tom Inglesby, director of the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security and the Bloomberg School of Public Health. He explains what has governments so worried and what measures could be put in place to reduce the risks
Could AI ‘change the stakes’ in the development of bioweapons?
Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘These risks are real’: the threat of AI bioweapons – podcast

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Eleanor Biggs and Rudi Zygadlo
articles.description:
The bestselling author says her books will no longer be supplied to UK bookshops over fears of prosecution. Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique report
For now there might be a copy or two of Intermezzo left kicking around in your local bookshop – snap it up if you haven’t already, because soon that will be it.
